purpose: Define how each executable Routine step crosses the normal command/runtime dispatcher boundary, preserving per-step validation, authorization, result and failure semantics.

topics.name: Runner Step Dispatch
topics.purpose: Define how each executable Routine step crosses the normal command/runtime dispatcher boundary, preserving per-step validation, authorization, result and failure semantics.

semantics.resolve_rule: Step resolves exact command/operation identity and argument schema.
semantics.dispatch_rule: Effectful step invokes the normal runtime dispatcher.
semantics.authority_rule: Authorization/assurance is evaluated for the actual step operation; Routine approval does not silently grant all contained rights.
semantics.result_rule: Step result is stored as inert runner data unless an explicit later step consumes a declared value.
semantics.failure_rule: Step failure follows explicit stop/continue/retry policy.
semantics.retry_rule: Retries are bounded and cannot bypass authorization or capability failures.
semantics.trace_rule: Runner trace links each step to dispatch execution identity/result.

invariants.rule: Routine definitions and runner executions are separate canonical identities; runners execute explicit ordered routine content through the normal governed dispatch boundary.

hard_gates.condition: routine-level permission silently grants all step permissions

references.purpose: Routine steps use normal governed execution.
Step failures retain structured error semantics.
